name: Kelvex TacSling Courier Bag MK-3
description:
Single-strap ballistic-nylon messenger bag in transit-authority grey with high-vis orange reflective piping along the flap seam. The body is reinforced at corners with vulcanized rubber bumpers. Interior is a dense foam-lined main compartment with a rigid document sleeve and a secondary mesh pocket sized for a compact medkit.

The shoulder strap is wide, padded, and routes over the chest with a magnetic sternum clip that releases under pressure — designed for quick dismount in crowded transit cars. Exterior has a waterproof map sleeve and two zippered side pockets.
functionality: Waterproof main compartment, rigid document sleeve rated for A3 flatfiles, chest-release strap for rapid dismount, exterior RFID-shielded pocket for transit passes and ID chips. Fits over chrome arm rigs without binding.
what_it_says: This person moves fast, carries what matters, and doesn't have time to look precious about it.
story_hooks: The MK-3 has a manufacturing defect in the RFID shielding — corporate knows, and chose not to issue a recall.
A courier's bag was found abandoned on a MagRail platform, interior pristine except for a handwritten list of names — all Tier 4 executives.
Street vendors near Circuit stations sell knockoff MK-3s with a hidden secondary compartment built into the foam lining.
